    • Per-pair regression statistics with qtlRegressionStats

Linear regression statistics for a collection of SNP-gene pairs

Source: R/qtlRegressionStats.R
qtlRegressionStats.Rd

For each (phenotype_id, variant_id) pair, fits a linear model of phenotype on genotype plus all covariates stored in the tQTLExperiment and returns a tidy data frame of coefficients, standard errors, t-statistics, and p-values for every model term. Pairs are grouped by phenotype and processed in parallel via BiocParallel::bplapply().

Usage

qtlRegressionStats(
  tqe,
  pairs = NULL,
  symbol = NULL,
  window = 1000000L,
  assayName = NULL,
  t_only = TRUE,
  wideFormat = TRUE,
  BPPARAM = BiocParallel::SerialParam()
)

Arguments

tqe

A tQTLExperiment with genotype data.

pairs

A data frame with columns phenotype_id and variant_id identifying the SNP-gene pairs to analyse. Mutually exclusive with symbol.

symbol

Character scalar. Gene symbol to look up in the gene_name column of rowRanges(tqe). All variants within window bp of the gene's start are used as the SNP set. The tQTLExperiment must have a gene_name column added via addGeneSymbols(); the function stops with an informative error if it is absent. Mutually exclusive with pairs.

window

Integer. Cis-window half-width in bp used when symbol is specified. Defaults to 1000000L.

assayName

Name of the assay to use. Defaults to the first assay.

t_only

Logical. If TRUE (default), return only the t-statistic (estimate / std.error) for each model term. In wide format columns are named <term>.t. If FALSE, return estimates and standard errors (and additionally statistic and p.value in long format).

wideFormat

Logical. If TRUE (default), pivot to one row per pair. With t_only = TRUE: one column per term named <term>.t. With t_only = FALSE: two columns per term, estimate.<term> and std.error.<term>. If FALSE, return the long tidy form with one row per pair x term.

BPPARAM

A BiocParallel::BiocParallelParam object controlling parallelisation. Defaults to BiocParallel::SerialParam() (single core). Use e.g. BiocParallel::MulticoreParam() for multicore.

Value

A data frame. See t_only and wideFormat for the shape of the output.

Details

Chromosome naming discrepancy. The rowRanges of a tQTLExperiment built from a SummarizedExperiment typically carries UCSC-style seqnames (e.g. "chr17"), while tqtlVariantRanges() reflects the PLINK BIM file convention of bare chromosome numbers (e.g. "17"). When symbol is used to select cis-variants, both seqname vectors are normalised by stripping any leading "chr" before comparison, so the window filter works regardless of which convention each source uses.

If you write code that compares or intersects rowRanges and tqtlVariantRanges directly, apply the same normalisation:


  sub("^chr", "", as.character(seqnames(gr)))

Examples

exdir <- system.file("extdata", package = "tQTLExperiment")
tqe <- tQTLExperiment(
    plinkPrefix = file.path(exdir, "chr22-n100"),
    phenoFile   = file.path(exdir, "mean-pheno-n100.bed"),
    covFile     = file.path(exdir, "cov-n100-tqtl.tsv"),
    genome      = "hg38"
)
#> Extracting number of samples and rownames from chr22-n100.fam...
#> Extracting number of variants and colnames from chr22-n100.bim...
pairs <- data.frame(
    phenotype_id = rownames(tqe)[1],
    variant_id   = S4Vectors::mcols(tqtlVariantRanges(tqe))[["snp_id"]][1]
)
qtlRegressionStats(tqe, pairs)
#>      phenotype_id     variant_id t._Intercept_ t.genotype         t.sex
#> 1 ENSG00000100181 22:16849573A-G      1.812558  -1.067511 -0.0003593606
#>        t.age t.expr_pc1 t.expr_pc2 t.geno_pc1 t.geno_pc2 t.geno_pc3 t.geno_pc4
#> 1 -0.7850642  -1.394788 -0.7426527   1.167902   1.021817   1.112029 -0.6122195
#>   t.geno_pc5 t.geno_pc6
#> 1  0.2154714   0.972025
qtlRegressionStats(tqe, pairs, t_only = FALSE, wideFormat = FALSE)
#>       phenotype_id     variant_id        term      estimate    std.error
